clue.text: Ground offensive left Rwanda struggling with food

indicators.note: something struggling is writhing about, so the letters of Rwanda are thrown into a new order

parts.note: fare is food, as in a bill of fare

explanation.surface: A news report of a ground offensive in Rwanda, its troops struggling for supplies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'struggling' rearranges the letters of Rwanda to give ANDWAR; 'with' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Warfare fought by armies across territory, as opposed to at sea or in the air, is a ground offensive.

clue.text: Heartless Soviet camp "in the way", in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: the shortened camp name is placed in the middle of the word for the way

parts.note: a lane is a way or road

indicators.note: losing its heart means the central letter of the camp's name is dropped

parts.note: the gulag was the Soviet system of labour camps

explanation.surface: A Soviet camp described, in quotation marks, as 'in the way', so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' removes the middle letter. The surface phrase 'in a manner of speaking' hides the definition inside a stock idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: A tongue such as French or English is a system of words, which is a way people speak.

clue.text: Skittles record I held in Northern pubs

indicators.note: the record and I are held inside the word for pubs

parts.note: inns are pubs
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: Someone recalls holding a record at skittles in pubs up north.
explanation.walkthrough: Skittles is a traditional British pub game of knocking down wooden pins with a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninepins is another name for the game of skittles, played by bowling at nine wooden pins.

clue.text: Matthau dropping line in lake

indicators.note: dropping means letting the letter for line fall out of the actor's first name

parts.note: Walter Matthau was an American film actor

explanation.surface: The actor Walter Matthau drops a fishing line in a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking L out of WALTER leaves the answer; 'in' just links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A lake is a large body of standing water, so the word for its substance can stand for it.

clue.text: Free to sign a new rental agreement

definitions.meaning: to free a prisoner is to let them go
to let a property again under a fresh contract, read as re- plus lease

explanation.surface: A landlord offers a tenant something free in exchange for signing a new lease.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the word as RE-LEASE, to lease again.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: letting go is the ordinary meaning, and leasing again is the hyphenated reading.

clue.text: Current Hair star?

parts.note: AC is alternating current
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Asks who is currently starring in the musical Hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hair' looks like the title of the musical, which suits the star, but it is just a lock of hair, TRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A leading female performer on stage or screen is often called a star; the question mark admits it is an example.

clue.text: Former English politician into new kind of relief

parts.note: ex- means former
MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: new tells us the word into is remade with its letters in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A former English politician moves into some new kind of benefit or relief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' looks like a link word but is the fodder that 'new' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Being let off a tax or duty is tax relief, a particular type of freedom from an obligation.

clue.text: Spot Fox going into retirement

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing backwards, so the fox's word is read in reverse

parts.note: tod is an old and dialect word for a fox

explanation.surface: A sighting of a fox heading off to bed, or a retired TV presenter called Fox.
explanation.walkthrough: TOD for fox is a crossword staple; reversed it gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A small round mark is a spot, as in a polka dot.

clue.text: Get rid of the new PM — reject old rubbish!

parts.note: the prefix de- means removing something, as in delouse

indicators.note: to reject is to throw out, so the letter for old is thrown out

parts.note: Boris Johnson became Prime Minister in July 2019, just before this puzzle

explanation.surface: A political rallying cry: oust the new Prime Minister and throw out the old rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get rid of the new PM' is DE-BORIS; 'reject' then removes the O. The PM is topical: Boris Johnson took office weeks before publication.
explanation.definitionFit: Scattered fragments and remains left after destruction are a kind of waste or junk.

clue.text: They have a revenue stream, thanks to Magneto et al

parts.note: ta is informal British for thanks
Magneto and his fellow mutants are the X-Men of Marvel comics

explanation.surface: Marvel's mutants are credited with generating a lucrative film franchise.
explanation.walkthrough: A revenue stream sounds like the X-Men's box office, but the collectors of revenue are meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Tax collectors gather the state's revenue, so an income stream flows through them.

clue.text: Sign of confidence in acrobat group?

definitions.meaning: performing with no safety net beneath shows an acrobat's confidence
a group of nine musicians, the question mark flagging the split reading

explanation.surface: Wonders whether a circus troupe shows its confidence by working without a net.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as NO NET for the acrobat; whole, it is an ensemble of nine.
explanation.definitionFit: An ensemble of nine players or a piece for nine instruments is a specific musical grouping.

clue.text: Through which to deliver improved hair, according to Spooner

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the first sounds of the two words change places

parts.note: something improved is better
locks are hair

explanation.surface: Suggests a Spoonerism about getting improved hair delivered.
explanation.walkthrough: BETTER LOCKS with the B and L swapped becomes LETTER BOCKS, which is spelt as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Post is pushed through the slot in a front door, which is where a postman delivers mail.

clue.text: Secure app developed, written as FORTRAN?

indicators.note: software that is developed is built up anew, so the letters of secure app are rearranged

explanation.surface: A programmer writes a secure app in the FORTRAN programming language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' and FORTRAN suggest coding, but the definition points to the capitals the name is printed in.
explanation.definitionFit: FORTRAN is traditionally spelt entirely in capital letters, which is the typographic case being described.

clue.text: First-rate, formal English

parts.note: prim means stiffly formal and proper

explanation.surface: Praises something as first-rate, formal English.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-quality goods are described as of the best grade, as in prime beef.

clue.text: Began a cheesecake filled with chocolate cream

indicators.note: the phrase is filled with the answer, which sits inside its letters

explanation.surface: Someone started a cheesecake with a chocolate cream filling.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth mixture of melted chocolate and cream used for fillings and icings.

clue.text: Organic bananas planted on random, deserted peak in the highlands

indicators.note: in a down clue the rearranged letters are planted on top of the second piece
bananas is slang for crazy, so the letters of organic go wild
a deserted word is emptied of everything but its outer letters

explanation.surface: Organic bananas grown at random on an empty Scottish mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' looks like fruit but scrambles ORGANIC to CAIRNGO; 'deserted' leaves RM of 'random'. The Cairngorms are a mountain range in the Scottish Highlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Cairn Gorm is a mountain in the Scottish Highlands that gives its name to the surrounding range.

clue.text: A-list rejected an oik like Pte Walker

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: the A-list are VIPs, very important people

explanation.surface: A celebrity crowd snubs a lowly oik.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Walker is the black-market wide boy in the British TV sitcom Dad's Army; 'oik' is British slang for a vulgar lout.
explanation.definitionFit: A flashy petty dealer in black-market goods is a type of British wartime character, as Walker was.

clue.text: Revolting, bitter bile uncovered in lyrical works

indicators.note: revolting means turning over, so the remaining letters are read backwards
uncovered strips the outside letters from the phrase, exposing the run inside it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Something disgusting, bitter bile, is exposed in poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'uncovered in' as part of the definition; 'uncovered' is the instruction that strips the outer B and E, and 'in' only links. 'Revolting' turns the remaining ITTERBIL round.
explanation.definitionFit: The texts of operas, sung words set to music, are plural lyrical works.

clue.text: Being a plant, I must leave "Hail, Spode!" movement

indicators.note: the letter I has to leave the pool of letters before they are rearranged
a movement of the letters of the quoted greeting signals that they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A speaker quits the 'Hail, Spode!' movement, the fascist Black Shorts led by Roderick Spode in P. G. Wodehouse.
explanation.walkthrough: HAILSPODE less I is rearranged to give the answer. 'Being a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A lily-family flower associated in Greek myth with the fields of the dead.

clue.text: Select a tool

definitions.meaning: a pointed digging tool, as in a pickaxe

explanation.surface: Choose an implement.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb sense means choose, and the noun sense is the pointed iron tool used for breaking ground.

clue.text: Merkel getting the shakes, taking a tablet in government building

indicators.note: shaking up the letters of the German chancellor's surname rearranges them
taking the tablet removes it from the letters before they are rearranged

parts.note: Angela Merkel, then German Chancellor
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet

explanation.surface: Angela Merkel shakes and takes a pill in a government building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' looks like adding, but here the tablet is taken away before 'getting the shakes' rearranges the remaining KREML; either E may go.
explanation.definitionFit: The fortified Moscow complex houses the Russian presidency and is shorthand for the Russian government.

clue.text: Simple souls process number two, having spent a penny

indicators.note: to process is to work over, so the letters of the other solution are rearranged
spending the penny means it is gone from the pool of letters

parts.note: 2-down is the clue numbered two, whose solution is the game of skittles
P is the abbreviation for a penny

explanation.surface: A lavatorial joke: after spending a penny, one deals with a number two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number two' means the answer to 2-down, not the toilet sense. Remove P from it and rearrange. 'Spending a penny' is British slang for using a public toilet, which once cost a penny.
explanation.definitionFit: Foolish, simple-minded people are called fools or simpletons, simple souls in kinder words.

clue.text: Humours original word for buttocks being circulated

indicators.note: the buttocks word goes round the word for original

parts.note: nates is the anatomical Latin word for the buttocks
ur- is a prefix meaning original, as in Urtext

explanation.surface: Someone circulates an old and original rude word for buttocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Humours' is a plural noun, temperaments, not a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Old medicine held that a person's temperament came from their bodily fluids, so temperaments and dispositions match.

clue.text: Girlie regularly featured in text looks happy

indicators.note: the picked letters are featured inside the word for a text

parts.note: SMS is a text message

indicators.note: taking regular letters picks every other one from the word girlie

explanation.surface: A girlish emoji in a text suggests happiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the second, fourth and sixth letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To beam or grin is to show pleasure on the face, so it is a verb of looking cheerful.

clue.text: Second Wolverine catchphrase …

parts.note: Logan is the real name of the Marvel superhero Wolverine

explanation.surface: A second catchphrase for the X-Men's Wolverine, continued in the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A memorable motto or advertising phrase is a catchword, a phrase people repeat.

clue.text: Chaps downing limoncello on vacation — it's quite sweet

indicators.note: downing a drink takes it inside, so the emptied liqueur goes into the chaps

parts.note: chaps are men

indicators.note: a vacated word has been emptied, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: Holidaying men knocking back the sweet lemon liqueur limoncello.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' empties the liqueur's name to its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The juicy fruit, such as a cantaloupe or honeydew, has a mildly sugary flesh.

clue.text: Skinny bloke to sit more than half of next day in city pub

indicators.note: the shortened word sits inside the city and pub letters
the shortened word goes in between the other letters

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London
PH is the abbreviation for public house

indicators.note: keeping more than half the letters of the word means its last three are cut off

parts.note: tomorrow is the next day

explanation.surface: A thin man plans to spend most of tomorrow sitting in a City pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'more than half of' keeps five of the eight letters, leaving TOMOR; EC is the City of London's postcode.
explanation.definitionFit: A person of slender, light build is a body type in Sheldon's classification of physiques.

clue.text: … second to struggle with film

parts.note: mo is short for moment, a second
to vie is to struggle or compete

explanation.surface: Continues the Wolverine theme: a second struggle on film.
explanation.definitionFit: A motion picture is a film, with the words interchangeable for a cinema release.

clue.text: One scratching the back of lumberjack?

definitions.meaning: a politician who trades favours, you scratch my back and I'll scratch yours
a person who rolls felled logs, with the question mark for the literal reading

explanation.surface: A lumberjack scratching his own back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' links the two senses. Logrolling is trading political favours or votes.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: the favour-trading politician and the worker who rolls timber in a river.

clue.text: Very old Irish priest made his mark

parts.note: Father Ted is the Irish priest of the TV sitcom

explanation.surface: An elderly Irish priest has made his mark on the world.
explanation.walkthrough: Father Ted is a well-known British comedy series about a priest on an Irish island.
explanation.definitionFit: Marking a cross on a ballot paper is how one casts a choice in an election.

clue.text: Star is suing every now and again

indicators.note: only now and again means picking alternate letters from the phrase

explanation.surface: A celebrity goes to law every so often.
explanation.definitionFit: Our nearest stellar body is the star at the centre of the solar system.

clue.text: After conversion, I'm saintlier (like the vicar)

indicators.note: a conversion changes form, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: A convert boasts of being holier than the vicar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conversion' suggests religion, fitting the vicar, but signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the clergy and their office, as a vicar's ministry does.
